verdicts.rationale: Both entries are 'Symbolic Gesturing in Normal Infants', Acredolo & Goodwyn 1988, Child Development 59(2):450, same DOI. Only the bibtex type differs (incollection vs article).

Both members carry identical fields: 'Organizational conflict and mental health service system effectiveness', Grusky & Adams 1994, same DOI. Citekeys mention 'fodorian' but both bib records describe the same (mental-health) work identically, so the two members are the same entry.

Same title/authors (Schacter & Addis). Second member is a reprint in the edited volume 'Mental Processes in the Human Brain' with a chapter DOI; its note explicitly cites the 2007 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B original. Same underlying work.
Identical fields: 'Perceptual Organization and the Judgment of Brightness', Adelson 1993, Science 262(5142):2042-2044, same DOI.
Both 'Spatiotemporal energy models for the perception of motion', Adelson & Bergen 1985, JOSA A vol 2, p.284. Same work; second is an abbreviated citation.
Identical: 'Aspect, agreement and measure phrases in Scottish Gaelic', Adger 1996, same booktitle/pages/DOI.
All four members are 'Size-contrast illusions deceive the eye but not the hand', Aglioti/DeSouza/Goodale 1995, Current Biology 5(6):679-685, same DOI.
Both 'Shape recognition and inferior temporal neurons', Schwartz/Desimone/Albright/Gross 1983, PNAS 80:5776-5778, same DOI.
Both 'Analyzing intention in utterances', Allen & Perrault 1980, Artificial Intelligence 15(3):143-178, same DOI. Second just adds a reprint note.
Both 'Film Theory and Philosophy', Allen & Smith, same publisher and ISBN 9780198159889.
Both 'Mapping human visual cortex with positron emission tomography', Fox et al. 1986, Nature 323(6091):806-809, same DOI.
Both 'Themes from Kaplan', 1989 Oxford edited volume (Almog/Perry/Wettstein). First member's note documents it was resolved from a review to the volume itself; both now describe the same book.
Both 'Innocent exclusion in an Alternative Semantics', Alonso-Ovalle, NLS 16(2):115-128, same DOI. Citekeys differ only by a truncated suffix.
Both 'If pictures are stative, what does this mean for discourse interpretation?', Altshuler & Schlöder 2021, SuB 25:19-36, same DOI.

Both 'How many objects can you track?', Alvarez & Franconeri 2007, Journal of Vision 7(13):14, same DOI.
